answer: Each epoch the protocol posts U, already-finalized txs still free as witnesses. A first-seen key must cite k distinct finalized txs from unrelated keys, k = 1 plus first-seen submits already included, and each cited relic is consumed this epoch. One joiner cites 1; after nine new keys the tenth cites 10, so the next head costs more (triangle n(n+1)/2). U cannot be reset, split, or pre-aged: only other keys' old finalized txs count, one citation per tx, citations die at close. Refuse them and the submit is dropped. An unused-parent oasis shrinks as the river of new keys serializes.
